title: Pullback preserves communication complexity
statement: Let $p$ be a finite-message deterministic communication protocol over input types $X$ and $Y$ with output type $\alpha$, and let $f_X : X' \to X$ and $f_Y : Y' \to Y$ be maps of input types. Then the pullback protocol obtained by precomposing every message function of $p$ with $f_X$ or $f_Y$ (as appropriate) has the same communication complexity as $p$.
hypotheses_covered: p a finite-message protocol over X, Y with output type α
replaced:
The pullback does not change the communication complexity:
$(p.\mathrm{comap}\,f_X\,f_Y).\mathrm{complexity} = p.\mathrm{complexity}$.
